messages:
maria: Customer (acct: acme-inc) reports repeated 502/504 on hosted streaming endpoint under load. They attach req id rq_a9c4f77d and say failures spike when they open ~80 concurrent streams.

josh: Which route/model and approximate timestamps? Any infra deploys right before?

maria: Route /v1/stream/complete, model: redwood-llama-lite. Timestamps: 2026-07-02T10:12:30Z to 10:13:05Z. Deploy-bot shows no deploys in that window.

anya: Can we get the client's curl or python trace and the request-id? Need to map to gateway logs.

maria: They shared a curl trace snippet and one client stack: 
``
* Connected to api.redwood.ai
> GET /v1/stream/complete HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-request-id: rq_a9c4f77d
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
```

elia: Ops metrics show a short spike of upstream 503s for auth-proxy around 10:12Z on gateway node gw-18. Also envoys on gw-18 show active_streams hitting the configured http2 max of 96.

ryan: Possible combo: (1) upstream auth-proxy transient errors; (2) HTTP/2 stream ceiling hit causing resets; (3) keepalive/idle interplay for long-lived client streams.

anya: If active_streams >= max_concurrent_streams, Envoy rejects or resets new streams. We should pull the admin stats for gw-18: active_streams, http2.rx_active, upstream_rq_pending, upstream_rq_503.

opsbot: [alert] upstream_service=auth-proxy instance=auth-3 status=503 count=9 window=60s node=gw-18

elia: I pulled the admin dump. active_streams peaked at 102 while http2.max_concurrent_streams was 96. upstream_rq_pending had a short queue, then upstream_rq_503 increased.

josh: Short-term mitigation: (A) bump http2 max_concurrent_streams on gw-18 to 192 and increase auth upstream connection pool; (B) enable a fast-fail circuit-breaker for route when auth-proxy 5xx rate exceeds threshold. Target a one-node change first.

maria: Customer asked if something changed client-side; they did not rotate tokens. We rolled an infra header tweak earlier today but timing doesn't align. Seems capacity / pool exhaustion.

ryan: Agreed. Also ask customer to reduce concurrent streams to ~30 as a stopgap while we mitigate. Request their client-side logs if failures continue.

elia: I applied a targeted config bump and restarted worker process on gw-18 (graceful reload). Monitoring now.

opsbot: task #INF-4982 created to increase http2 concurrency across the gw pool and add auth upstream pool capacity. Assigned to eng-sre.

maria: After the gw-18 reload, customer reports a big drop in 502s for ~25 minutes. We'll roll the config to the remaining gw nodes slowly.

anya: Follow-ups: (1) instrument per-route long-lived stream counts and auth lookup latency; (2) implement a local LRU token cache (TTL) at gateway layer to reduce auth-proxy pressure; (3) automatic per-node backpressure when auth error rate > 1.5%.

ryan: Also schedule a load test that simulates 200 concurrent streaming clients to validate changes. Assign to eng-runtime + eng-sre.

maria: I'll send the customer an incident update: short RCA (auth-proxy overload + http2 stream limit reached), mitigation steps (bumped concurrency, added circuit-breaker, targeted restart), and client guidance. Will attach req ids and ask for any further repro traces.

opsbot: ticket INC-4982 created for customer comms and RCA tracking.

maria: Closing thread for now; will reopen if we see recurrence. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
